title: A bank people talk about
line: Roughly 100 followers to over 10,000 in nine months.
brief: VFD had a working product and almost no audience. Around a hundred followers, a feed that read like a press office, and a market where a bank is chosen on whether it feels trustworthy in the first ten seconds of a scroll.
approach: We stopped publishing announcements and started publishing reasons. One voice, a weekly content engine built around what customers actually ask, and a posting rhythm the team could hold without us. Every format was designed to be understood on mute.
outcome: Roughly a hundred followers to over ten thousand in nine months, and a feed the client's own staff started sharing.

title: Capri-Sonne summer
line: A seasonal campaign built to travel across every format.
brief: Capri-Sonne needed a summer campaign that would hold together across shelf, screen and street without being rebuilt for each one.
approach: One art direction, built as a system rather than a key visual — a palette, a crop logic and a type treatment that survive being cut to a billboard, a six-second bumper and a shelf wobbler.
outcome: A single campaign look that ran across every format without a redesign for each placement.

title: Insurance without the flinch
line: Life cover explained the way people actually ask about it.
brief: Life insurance is sold in language most people flinch at. Prudential Zenith needed to be understood by people who had never bought cover and were not sure they wanted to think about why they might need it.
approach: We rewrote the proposition around the question customers actually ask, then built an identity and campaign warm enough to carry it. No small print as a personality.
outcome: A brand line and campaign system the sales team could use without translating it first.

title: The whole range, one voice
line: Twelve products held together by a single art direction.
brief: Twelve products, twelve looks. Chivita's range had grown faster than the art direction holding it together, and on shelf it read as a dozen brands rather than one.
approach: A single art direction applied across the whole range — one light, one crop logic, one way fruit behaves — so each product stays itself while the range reads as a family.
outcome: A range that holds together on a shelf and in a grid.

title: Clean energy, plainly put
line: Solar sold on the evening it gives back, not on the hardware.
brief: Solar in Nigeria is usually sold on hardware — panel counts, inverter ratings, warranty years. ESVolt needed to reach people who do not want a specification, they want the evening back.
approach: We moved the argument off the equipment and onto the outcome. The campaign leads with the hours it gives you, and the technical case sits underneath for the people who go looking.
outcome: A campaign that sells the evening rather than the inverter.

title: Banking that fits the thumb
line: A fintech brand that had to earn trust in ten seconds.
brief: Dash MFB had ten seconds to earn trust from someone holding a phone who had never heard of them, in a market with good reasons to be careful about a new bank.
approach: An identity built for a small screen first, and a product surface where the reassuring details — who holds the money, what it costs, how to get it out — arrive before the marketing does.
outcome: A brand that reads as a bank at thumbnail size.

title: Counsel with a spine
line: A law firm positioned on conviction rather than credentials.
brief: Most law firms introduce themselves with credentials. Acacia wanted to be chosen for conviction, which is a much harder thing to put on a letterhead.
approach: We positioned the firm on the way it argues rather than the schools it went to, and built an identity with enough spine to carry that without shouting.
outcome: A firm that sounds like itself in a category that mostly sounds the same.

title: Power you can picture
line: Optoelectronics made legible to the people who buy it.
brief: Aurora sells optoelectronics to buyers who are not engineers. The existing material explained the technology and never explained the point.
approach: We rebuilt the story around what the product does for the person specifying it, and made a content set that shows the thing working rather than the thing itself.
outcome: Technical products made legible to the people who actually sign for them.
